decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up right-hand approach to the key; keep left arm parked. Key is nearer the center than in the reference.
Advance right arm in a smooth elbow-up arc while pitching the open gripper toward a top-down grasp.
Replan after continuity rejection with reduced increments; continue toward the key without compensating discarded targets.
Move over the key and align the downward gripper to its visible diagonal shaft; maintain smooth configuration.
Complete top-down alignment over the bow/shaft junction; slow descent with gripper open for visual refinement.
Center the shaft between the fingers using the wrist view, then close without moving the key.
Allow the gripper to finish closing, then begin a short test lift and check retention visually.
Lift the visibly captured key clear of the table while holding the gripper fully closed.
Raise and yaw the retained key toward a central handover orientation, keeping the right hand on its own side.
Continue positioning the key for transfer while beginning the left arm's elbow-up receiving approach.
Bring the right-held key to transfer height and yaw, and advance the open left receiver through a raised elbow-up arc.
Continue the left receiving approach without crossing arms; hold the captured key steady at the transfer location.
Advance the left hand toward the exposed key bow while keeping the right grasp closed and stationary.
Finish orienting the left gripper horizontally toward the key bow; stop short for a careful transfer approach.
Reduce the final orientation increments after the guard rejection, then inch toward the bow with a partially open receiving gripper.
Slide the left fingertips toward the exposed bow along the key axis, leaving the right grasp unchanged.
Refine the receiving fingers slightly below and behind the bow after visible contact deflection; begin a gentle closure while the right hand retains it.
Reopen the receiver briefly, lower to center the visibly tilted bow, and seat it deeper before closing; keep the donor closed.
Finish seating and closing the left bow grasp, then progressively release the donor while watching for retention.
Keep the receiving grip closed and withdraw the open right hand cautiously; the key shifted during release, so retention needs visual confirmation.
The key slipped from the receiving fingers. Clear both hands and let it settle for a new grasp.
The key appears at the upper receiving fingertip; recenter the left grip upward and close while withdrawing the open donor.
The key is now on the table. Withdraw the left hand and begin a fresh right-hand approach aligned with its new diagonal orientation.
The settled key now lies nearly across the table. Descend over its shaft with the right fingers aligned across it.
Continue descending toward the settled shaft and correct its slight yaw, keeping the left hand clear.
Use the wrist image to center the opposite-facing shaft and lower to grasp height; the key is not yet retained.
Center the key neck in the right fingertips and close at table level for the recovery grasp.
Shift the right grasp off the round bow onto the shaft so the bow remains accessible for a better handover.
Finish the shaft pinch and test a small lift before attempting the adjusted handover.
Lift the recovered key and start rotating its bow toward the left receiver; verify it remains between the right fingers.
Raise the key toward receiver height and continue its in-place yaw adjustment with the donor fully closed.
The recovery grasp slipped during yaw. Reorient the open right hand so a new shaft grasp will already present the bow toward the receiver.
Approach the settled key with the open right gripper and align to its current diagonal, avoiding another loaded yaw.
Finish matching the unloaded right gripper to the shaft direction and descend in small increments.
Translate the open gripper over the visibly offset shaft while maintaining the matched yaw and elbow-up configuration.
Correct the remaining lateral shaft offset and visible yaw before closing; keep the right wrist on its own side.
The shaft is now between the right fingertips. Close without further yaw and give the receiver additional clearance.
Clear the left fingers away from the donor wrist, then test the new pinch with a short vertical lift and no yaw.
The key is off-center in the closed fingers. Reopen and gain clearance before correcting yaw, holding the left arm after its continuity rejection.
Lower with a small lateral correction and reverse the yaw refinement to center the neck in the wrist view before closure.
Match the gripper yaw to the now-stationary key at slight clearance, separating orientation refinement from contact.
Center the shaft at the fingertip pinch line while completing the small remaining yaw correction and descent.
The shaft is centered and upright in the wrist view. Close fully without translation or rotation.
Allow closure to settle, then use a minimal vertical test lift to check whether the shaft is captured.
Lift straight upward with the shaft held closed; avoid yaw until retention is clear.
The key hangs from the captured teeth. Raise it without rotation so the left hand can approach the exposed bow below the donor.
Raise the retained hanging key and bring the open receiver toward the lower bow, with ample lateral separation.
Center the hanging bow in the left wrist view by lowering the receiver and approaching slowly; retain the donor grip.
The teeth grasp has slipped. Separate the hands and reopen the donor before a deeper shaft recovery grasp.
Approach the middle of the settled shaft with the open right hand, preserving clearance from the left receiver.
Descend toward a neck grasp while aligning to the key's reversed orientation; no contact closure yet.
Lower over the centered neck, positioning the bow just above the pinch region rather than gripping the teeth.
Shift the pinch from the round bow to the straight neck, settle at grasp height, then close without yaw.
Let the fingers fully close, then make only a small test lift to determine where the key is retained.
The closed fingers missed the neck. Reopen and shift the pinch point farther down the shaft before another closure.
Place the straight shaft deeper in the pinch region, away from the round bow, and close at the lower grasp height.
Complete closure around the centered shaft and test retention with only a four-millimeter lift.
Lift the newly centered shaft grasp vertically, keeping the wrist orientation fixed and checking for slip.
Clear the left fingers from the donor wrist after visible interference, while keeping the newly captured key stationary and closed.
Reduce the left retreat and orientation increments after the continuity rejection; preserve the right grasp.
Lift the stable shaft pinch while slowly beginning to present its bow toward the receiver, keeping clear of the left fingers.
Continue the gradual lift and bow presentation; the shaft remains centered in the closed right fingers.
